facts.value: DOES NOT TIE. Paper: 'approximately £386k' at 31 December 2025 (Appendix A p.1). OUR file (price_book.py 'CHIPPENHAM TOWN COUNCIL (WILTS)' --as-at 2025-12-31): 1 loan outstanding, principal £70,743, weighted 3.8100%, ANNUITY. Gap of roughly £315k at the paper's stated reference date. At 2026-04-08 (date of the paper) our file shows 2 loans totalling £308,243 at a weighted 3.1397%, still £78k short of the £386k the paper reports for 31 December 2025.

facts.note: NAMING TRAP: the borrower name in our file is 'CHIPPENHAM TOWN COUNCIL (WILTS)' — --find 'Chippenham' returns exactly one match. The two individual PWLB loans in our file live at 2026-08-15: PW497435 ANNUITY £63,463 outstanding at 3.81% maturing 30 Jun 2030; PW504356 EIP £237,500 at 2.94% maturing 03 Sep 2035. The EIP appears between 2025-12-31 and 2026-04-08 in our file — a fresh Q1 2026 drawdown at a nominal 2.94% is not plausible on any PWLB certainty curve we hold, so a data-quality issue in our borrower ledger for this small borrower is the more likely explanation. Reconciliation gap recorded, no external claim made either way — per PIPELINE.md, a failed reconciliation is a note-only observation and never becomes part of an outbound email.

summary.text:
Chippenham Town Council's annual Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27 — a two-page covering report (doc 8554) plus a five-page Appendix A (doc 8590) — went to the Strategy & Resources Committee on 08 April 2026. The covering report explicitly states the strategy 'contains no significant changes from the previous strategy' (§3.1), and both papers together carry only three council-specific book numbers: 'approximately £386k of borrowing' at 31 December 2025, an investment-balance range of £3.5m to £5m during the year, and a CCLA Property Investment Fund holding of about £200k. There is no loan-by-loan schedule, no weighted average rate on the debt, no maturity profile, no CFR, no Authorised Limit or Operational Boundary, no MRP policy statement and no other prudential indicator anywhere in either paper.

Chippenham is a town (parish-tier) council. None of the omissions above are paper deficiencies — the CIPFA Prudential Code as normally structured does not apply to parish/town councils in the same way, and the strategy is prepared under Arlingclose advice on that basis ('applied proportionally to its size and level of activity' — covering report §2.1). The delegation is held by the RFO (styled 'Section 151 Officer / Responsible Financial Officer (RFO)' throughout the paper), acting with the Chief Executive, but under LGA 1972 town councils have no statutory s151 officer and the RFO role sits under section 112. The counterparty framework (Appendix A Table 3, p.4) is scaled to that world — £2m per LA on a two-year tenor, £1m each for banks/building societies/secured/pooled funds on a one-year tenor, £3m per MMF, unlimited UK Government on five years, minimum A- long-term rating.

Loan-book reconciliation does not tie. The paper reports 'approximately £386k' at 31 December 2025 (Appendix A p.1); our PWLB file for 'CHIPPENHAM TOWN COUNCIL (WILTS)' at that date shows one loan of £70,743 at 3.81% ANNUITY — a gap of about £315k. At the date of the paper itself (08 April 2026) our file shows two loans totalling £308,243, still short of the £386k. The second loan in our file (PW504356, EIP £237,500 at a nominal 2.94% maturing 03 September 2035) appears between 31 December 2025 and 08 April 2026, but a fresh Q1 2026 drawdown at 2.94% is not plausible on any PWLB certainty curve we hold, so a data-quality issue in our borrower ledger for this small borrower is the more likely explanation than a genuine mid-year drawdown at a sub-market rate. Neither the paper nor our own file is confidently the correct picture; per PIPELINE.md, a failed reconciliation is a note-only observation and does not become part of an outbound email. The balance-sheet identity is not testable — the paper prints no CFR and no OLTL — recorded as missing rather than derived.

No email is drafted from this document. The direct precedent is Barnstaple Town Council (mg474): a parish-tier authority sits outside the platform's target audience (S151 officers of principal authorities managing multi-hundred-million-pound treasury books), the paper contains no council-specific treasury content that would land as an interesting hook at that scale, the reconciliation does not tie so it cannot open with a match either, the named officer is the Director of Finance / RFO rather than a statutory s151 officer, and no email address is printed anywhere in either paper. A first-contact email here would misfire on audience and on material. The note records what the paper says, what our file says, and the gap between them, in case the borrower ledger is later cleaned up or the council's own paper is superseded by a fuller mid-year or outturn report.
